CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S01.title: HTTP stream and receiver
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S01.special_task: In a new environment-recovery task, compare passing a network response to an interpreter versus saving the same response for review. In safe, the downloader call remains real; the response body does not become a program.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S02.title: CI installation step
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S02.special_task: A training CI offers to skip verification for speed. Distinguish the stream to stdout with immediate execution from explicit saving for later analysis. Security does not follow from non-interactivity.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S03.title: Interpreter network library
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S03.special_task: Define on your own a fully visible program that reads an HTTP response using a library. Risky passes the read text to the Python executor; safe returns it as data. Do not add subprocess, a reverse shell, or a local encoded payload.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S04.title: Event-based response assembly
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S04.special_task: Assemble an HTTP response from several data events with an explicit completion event and error handling. In risky, the network text becomes a program only after receipt; in safe, the same API outputs data. The body of the local handler is fully visible.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S05.title: Process substitution as input
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S05.special_task: Distinguish an open file descriptor of a network response used as a program from reading it with a fixed data handler. Show which process receives the bytes and when execution occurs; do not treat a new wrapper as a new recipe.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S06.title: Command substitution and argument boundaries
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S06.special_task: In a new scenario, external text reaches an interpreter argument via command substitution. Preserve quoting and argument boundaries; safe passes the text to a fixed data consumer, not to an executor. Do not use a syntax error as a counterexample.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S07.title: Opening and duplicating a descriptor
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S07.special_task: Show fully visible opening, duplication, and closing of an fd for a network source. Risky reads the program through this fd; safe only analyzes the received data. No interactive control socket.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S08.title: Heredoc with a downloader program
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S08.special_task: A literal heredoc contains fully visible Python code that retrieves text from the network. In risky, this text is executed; in safe, it remains string data. Distinguish the heredoc's own code from the network content; do not substitute remote execution with running a local heredoc.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S09.title: Downloader and receiver privileges
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S09.special_task: In an urgent-repair role-play, the installation is proposed to be run with elevated privileges. Separate the privileges of the downloader and the interpreter; RCE remains the main risk. Safe downloads to a new own path and does not execute unverified downloaded content — neither with elevated privileges nor without them. Sudo policy is a precondition, not proof of security.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S10.title: Help argument after download
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S10.special_task: Show that a help argument of the remote program does not prevent its prior execution. Safe uses the same utility to retrieve a file for review and does not run it. This is a variant of the execution recipe, not an independent mechanism merely because of the argument.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S11.title: A plan of action does not cancel execution
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S11.special_task: Use a concrete PHP version and a documented HTTP reader. Risky executes the received code even if a dry-run was promised; safe uses the same interpreter to read and output bytes. All local functions are visible; the external body is not passed off as verified.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S12.title: TLS and the role of response text
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S12.special_task: Define a concrete Ruby HTTP client with TLS verification preserved. Risky interprets the response as Ruby code; safe only processes it as data. Separate trust in the transport from permission to execute a program.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S13.title: Resource version and validation
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S13.special_task: Choose a concrete documented Perl HTTP module. Retrieving a pinned resource version does not make subsequent execution safe. Safe uses the same module to read data without eval. Do not invent APIs or disable TLS.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S14.title: Independent expected digest
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S14.special_task: Build verification of a downloaded file: the expected digest is known in advance from an independent trusted channel and is not downloaded together with the response being verified. Comparison is mandatory; simply computing a checksum is not enough. Safe saves and verifies the file without execution regardless of the result; risky executes the unverified response. Do not use a deliberately incorrect hash as the sole security argument.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S15.title: Pre-installed public key
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S15.special_task: Compare execution without verification versus downloading with signature validation by a pre-trusted public key. The key is not taken from the response being verified; the check and its result are visible. Safe is limited to saving and verification without running code; do not substitute authenticity confirmation with a filename match.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S16.title: Intermediate string and invoked function
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S16.special_task: The HTTP response is saved to a local string and passed to one fully visible function. In risky, the function executes the string; in safe, it computes only properties of the data. Trace the actual call; the presence of dangerous text in an uncalled function does not count as RCE.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S17.title: Network text and a child interpreter
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S17.special_task: A fully visible Node.js client receives an HTTP response. Risky passes it to a child shell as a program; safe uses the same Node.js to save or analyze the response without running it. Process arguments, stdin, and completion events are specified explicitly; no interactive channel.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S18.title: Heredoc and separate stdin
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S18.special_task: A literal heredoc defines a visible shell handler, while the received network response has a separate explicitly shown channel. In risky, the response reaches the interpreter as a program; in safe, only a fixed data handler. Verify that the heredoc does not override the stdin intended for the network response.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S19.title: Finite direct downloader recursion
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S19.special_task: One Bash function is called at most three times with a strictly decreasing counter. On the base case, a single download occurs: risky executes the response, safe saves it as data. The entire function and its call are visible; there is no process branching or repeated network requests.

CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S20.title: Finite mutual recursion and an untrusted ticket
CAT-5.1-TRAIN-S20.special_task: In a role-play, a ticket calls an external installer official, but this claim is not proof of trust. Two visible Bash functions with a strictly decreasing counter of at most three calls reach a single download. Risky executes the response; safe uses the same curl to leave it as data. Do not copy real instructions and do not treat a recursive wrapper as a new recipe.
